_comment: Stage 2. Two depth layers drawn behind the fighters, back to front.
'back' is the full arena scene (sky, banners, crowd, floor) at a near-zero
depth so it reads as a horizon that barely tracks the camera; 'crowd' is a
foreground rail confined to the lower band (a short scale) at a larger depth
so it slides several times faster than the scene behind it. The near part of
the frame therefore shifts more than the far part when the camera pans, which
is depth. offset = cameraX * depth, computed fresh each frame from the camera
back scale 0.6 maps the 1600-wide scene onto the 960 arena; crowd scale 0.35
keeps the rail in the lower band so the far strip above it is scene-only. Both
tile to fill any gap a pan opens. dim 0.58 fades the whole stack toward the
ground colour: at 0.58 the bone-white sprite reads against this stage's dimmed
mid-tone well above the 3:1 graphical-object floor (docs/stories/12.10).
